thread:
maria: Heads-up — customer 'AcmeHealth' opened an escalation: sudden p95/p99 latency spike after we rolled the new quantization profile (int8) for model rwd-alpha-7b in us-west1. They reported increased tail latency and some auth retries.

ajay: Copy. Do we have the dashboard link or request_ids?

maria: Dashboard: https://console.redwood/acme/observability?panel=latency (shared). p95 went from ~420ms -> ~1.2s, p99 ~880ms -> ~3.6s after the profile deploy around 2026-03-16T08:03Z. Sample req ids: req_20260316_abc123, req_20260316_def456. Customer says their traffic is mostly short prompts (avg tokens 24).

luis: Quick guesses: int8 path could have changed kernel selection, and for short sequences batching/queueing might be worse if batch thresholds increased. Also check KV cache behavior — if the quantized variant invalidated some cache keys we could be recomputing more.

jamie: Running a trace query now: `curl -s "https://internal-api/trace?req=req_20260316_abc123" | jq .`

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout quant-profile/rwd-alpha-7b-int8 started by @ml-release at 2026-03-16T08:02:11Z.

ajay: Can someone check model runtime logs around those req ids for nvprof / kernel selection notes? Also verify batcher stats (avg batch size, batch wait time) for the canary pool.

luis: Grabbed batcher metrics for canary pool: avg_batch_size dropped from 6 -> 2. avg_batch_wait increased from 12ms -> 95ms during spike window. That explains latency. Seems like the quantized variant lowered throughput per-GPU causing smaller batches under same inflight requests.

maria: Interesting — customer traffic is bursty; our autoscaler/batcher thresholds may be mismatched for the int8 variant. Any quick mitigations?

sre-oncall: Mitigation options: 1) Freeze canary / rollback quant profile to previous fp16 profile for the affected model in us-west1. 2) Force fallback to fp16 at routing layer for Acme tenant. 3) Adjust batcher config temporarily (lower batch wait threshold) — but risk increased compute cost. Which do we prefer for low-friction?

ajay: I recommend 1 and 2 in parallel: freeze canary + tenant-level fp16 fallback. That should restore baseline quickly. We'll open a follow-up to tune batching and quant profile.

jamie: Actioning rollback now: `PATCH /admin/models/rwd-alpha-7b/profiles/canary` payload `{ "active_profile": "fp16-baseline" }` — returning 200.

ops-bot: config-bot: Model profile rollback applied to canary pool at 2026-03-16T08:12:47Z by jamie.

maria: Also enabled tenant-level override for Acme to force fp16 until we complete investigation: `POST /admin/tenants/acme/overrides {"model":"rwd-alpha-7b","profile":"fp16-baseline","reason":"latency spike"}` — 201 created.

luis: Re-checking metrics post-rollback: within ~3 minutes p95 back to ~450ms, p99 ~920ms — close to pre-rollout. avg_batch_size back to ~5, avg_batch_wait ~15ms.

ajay: Great. Root cause hypothesis: int8 profile changed execution kernel/latency characteristics for short-sequence workloads which reduced per-GPU effective throughput and interacted poorly with default batching thresholds. Also possible KV cache invalidation edge-case — need to verify whether int8 build enabled different KV cache key format/serialization.

jamie: Next steps: 1) Run controlled A/B with synthetic short-prompt workload against int8 variant with lowered batch wait threshold to measure p95/p99 and cost delta. 2) Verify cache key format for quantized builds. 3) Update rollout checklist to include short-prompt perf smoke tests and batcher threshold validation.

maria: Noted. I'll notify Acme support that we've rolled back and put a temporary fp16 override. I'll also ask CS to coordinate a private test window if they want to try the int8 again.

sre-oncall: Logging follow-up ticket: SRE-3421 — "Investigate int8 canary p99 regression for rwd-alpha-7b (us-west1)" with owner @luis.

maria: Thanks team — closing the customer escalation for now. Will reopen if they see anything else. :white_check_mark:
